title: Valuing the Teaching Profession I
source_note: Standard Nigerian university GST/teacher-education curriculum: nature and history of the teaching profession, TRCN and regulatory framework, National Policy on Education provisions for teacher training, professional ethics, qualities and roles of teachers, and challenges facing teaching in Nigeria.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines a 'profession' as distinct from an ordinary occupation?
options: Any job that pays a regular salary
A vocation requiring specialized knowledge, prolonged training, a code of ethics, and regulation by a professional body
Any work performed in an office setting
A job that does not require formal education
questions.correct_answer: A vocation requiring specialized knowledge, prolonged training, a code of ethics, and regulation by a professional body
questions.explanation: A profession is characterized by specialized knowledge, extended training, a code of ethics, and self-regulation through a recognized body, distinguishing it from a mere job.

questions.question: Which body is statutorily responsible for the registration and licensing of teachers in Nigeria?
options: National Universities Commission (NUC)
Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN)
National Examinations Council (NECO)
Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC)
questions.correct_answer: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN)
questions.explanation: TRCN is the statutory body charged with registering and licensing qualified teachers and regulating teaching practice in Nigeria.

questions.question: According to the National Policy on Education, what is the minimum teaching qualification for entry into the teaching profession in Nigeria?
options: West African Senior School Certificate (WASSCE)
Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE)
Ordinary National Diploma (OND)
First School Leaving Certificate
questions.correct_answer: Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE)
questions.explanation: The National Policy on Education stipulates the NCE as the minimum qualification for teaching in Nigeria.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT generally regarded as a core characteristic of a profession?
options: A specialized body of knowledge
A code of ethics guiding practitioners
Open entry with no training or certification required
A recognized professional association
questions.correct_answer: Open entry with no training or certification required
questions.explanation: Professions require formal training and certification; unrestricted entry without qualification is a hallmark of an unregulated occupation, not a profession.

questions.question: A teacher's code of professional ethics primarily serves to:
options: Guide acceptable conduct and maintain standards of practice among teachers
Determine the salary structure of teachers
Replace the need for a teaching qualification
Regulate the curriculum content taught in schools
questions.correct_answer: Guide acceptable conduct and maintain standards of practice among teachers
questions.explanation: A code of ethics sets out standards of professional conduct that practitioners are expected to uphold.

questions.question: Which of the following is a widely recognized quality of an effective teacher?
options: Favoritism towards certain students
Sound mastery of subject matter and effective communication skills
Reluctance to update teaching methods
Avoidance of student interaction outside class
questions.correct_answer: Sound mastery of subject matter and effective communication skills
questions.explanation: Effective teachers combine strong content knowledge with the ability to communicate it clearly to learners.

questions.question: The teacher-student relationship is best described as one that should be:
options: Purely authoritarian, with no room for dialogue
Built on mutual respect, trust, and guidance towards learning
Based solely on fear to maintain discipline
Distant and impersonal at all times
questions.correct_answer: Built on mutual respect, trust, and guidance towards learning
questions.explanation: A healthy teacher-student relationship fosters respect and trust, which supports effective learning and personal development.

questions.question: Which institution type was primarily established to train teachers at the certificate level before the widespread adoption of the NCE?
options: Teacher Training Colleges (Grade II)
Polytechnics
Federal Medical Centres
Agricultural Development Programmes
questions.correct_answer: Teacher Training Colleges (Grade II)
questions.explanation: Grade II Teacher Training Colleges historically produced certificated teachers before the NCE became the recognized minimum standard.

questions.question: Formal Western-style education, and with it organized teacher training, was first introduced into Nigeria mainly through:
options: Government decree after independence
Christian missionary activities in the 19th century
The establishment of federal universities
The Universal Basic Education programme
questions.correct_answer: Christian missionary activities in the 19th century
questions.explanation: Christian missionaries introduced formal Western education to Nigeria in the 19th century, establishing early schools and training arrangements for teachers.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'in-service training' for teachers?
options: Training given to teachers before they are employed
Continuous professional development undertaken by teachers while already in the job
Training reserved only for school administrators
A one-time orientation given only at the point of first employment
questions.correct_answer: Continuous professional development undertaken by teachers while already in the job
questions.explanation: In-service training refers to ongoing professional development activities for teachers who are already practicing.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major challenge commonly identified as facing the teaching profession in Nigeria?
options: Excessive prestige attached to the profession
Poor remuneration and inadequate incentives for teachers
Oversupply of instructional materials in all schools
Too many regulatory bodies overseeing teacher conduct
questions.correct_answer: Poor remuneration and inadequate incentives for teachers
questions.explanation: Low pay and weak incentives are frequently cited as key challenges undermining teacher motivation and the status of the profession in Nigeria.

questions.question: The primary trade union representing the interests of teachers in Nigeria is the:
options: Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU)
Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT)
Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) alone
Nigeria Medical Association (NMA)
questions.correct_answer: Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT)
questions.explanation: The NUT is the foremost professional union representing teachers, especially at the primary and secondary levels, in Nigeria.

questions.question: Which of the following is a legitimate function of a professional teaching body such as TRCN?
options: Setting the national minimum wage for all workers
Registering qualified teachers and sanctioning professional misconduct
Awarding university degrees
Determining the national school calendar
questions.correct_answer: Registering qualified teachers and sanctioning professional misconduct
questions.explanation: TRCN registers qualified teachers, maintains a professional register, and enforces disciplinary standards for misconduct.

questions.question: Teaching is often described as a 'noble profession' primarily because:
options: It offers the highest salaries among all professions
It shapes and influences the development of other professionals and society at large
It requires no specialized training
It has no code of ethics to follow
questions.correct_answer: It shapes and influences the development of other professionals and society at large
questions.explanation: Teaching is considered noble because teachers train and mould individuals who go on to become professionals in every other field.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of a teacher as a 'nation builder'?
options: Teachers only manage classroom discipline
Teachers instill knowledge, values, and skills that contribute to national development
Teachers are responsible for constructing school buildings
Teachers determine government economic policy
questions.correct_answer: Teachers instill knowledge, values, and skills that contribute to national development
questions.explanation: Teachers contribute to nation building by equipping learners with knowledge, skills, and values needed for national development.

questions.question: A key distinguishing feature between teaching and casual/unskilled work is that teaching requires:
options: No formal certification whatsoever
Specialized pedagogical training and subject mastery
Only physical strength
No engagement with learners
questions.correct_answer: Specialized pedagogical training and subject mastery
questions.explanation: Teaching demands trained expertise in both subject content and pedagogy, unlike unskilled work which requires neither.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of unprofessional conduct that would breach a teacher's code of ethics?
options: Preparing lesson notes in advance
Sexual harassment or exploitation of students
Giving extra help to a struggling student
Attending professional development workshops
questions.correct_answer: Sexual harassment or exploitation of students
questions.explanation: Sexual harassment of students is a serious violation of professional ethics and can lead to deregistration by regulatory bodies like TRCN.

questions.question: 'Vocation' in the context of teaching refers to:
options: A holiday period for teachers
A calling or strong inner commitment to the work of teaching
The physical location of a school
The examination body that certifies teachers
questions.correct_answer: A calling or strong inner commitment to the work of teaching
questions.explanation: Teaching is often described as a vocation because many practitioners see it as a calling rather than merely a source of income.

questions.question: Which factor most directly affects teacher motivation and commitment to the profession?
options: The colour of the school building
Remuneration, working conditions, and professional recognition
The number of holidays in the academic calendar alone
The size of the school compound
questions.correct_answer: Remuneration, working conditions, and professional recognition
questions.explanation: Motivation and commitment are strongly influenced by pay, working environment, and the degree of respect accorded to the profession.

questions.question: Colleges of Education in Nigeria primarily exist to:
options: Award postgraduate degrees in medicine
Train teachers to the NCE level
Conduct agricultural research
Regulate university admissions nationwide
questions.correct_answer: Train teachers to the NCE level
questions.explanation: Colleges of Education are dedicated institutions whose primary mandate is producing NCE-qualified teachers.

questions.question: A Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE) is designed mainly for:
options: Non-education graduates who wish to acquire teaching qualifications
Primary school pupils
School administrators with no degree
Only medical doctors
questions.correct_answer: Non-education graduates who wish to acquire teaching qualifications
questions.explanation: The PGDE allows graduates of non-education disciplines to gain the pedagogical qualification needed to teach professionally.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'professional accountability' for teachers?
options: Teachers being answerable for the quality of instruction and conduct in their duties
Teachers having no obligation to report to anyone
Only school principals being responsible for teaching outcomes
Accountability that applies only to private school teachers
questions.correct_answer: Teachers being answerable for the quality of instruction and conduct in their duties
questions.explanation: Professional accountability means teachers are responsible for their instructional quality and professional conduct to students, employers, and regulatory bodies.

questions.question: One major reason teaching in Nigeria is sometimes perceived as having lower status compared to other professions is:
options: Teachers have too much political power
Comparatively low pay and inconsistent professional recognition
Teaching requires no training at all
There are too few teachers in the country
questions.correct_answer: Comparatively low pay and inconsistent professional recognition
questions.explanation: Perceptions of low status are commonly linked to inadequate remuneration and inconsistent recognition relative to other professions.

questions.question: Which of the following best illustrates a teacher performing the role of a 'counselor'?
options: Grading examination scripts
Guiding a student through personal or academic difficulties
Preparing the school timetable
Collecting school fees
questions.correct_answer: Guiding a student through personal or academic difficulties
questions.explanation: Beyond instruction, teachers often support students' personal and academic wellbeing, functioning as informal counselors.

questions.question: A teacher acting as a 'role model' primarily influences students through:
options: Personal conduct and behavior that students observe and may emulate
The number of degrees the teacher holds
The teacher's physical appearance alone
Strict silence in the classroom
questions.correct_answer: Personal conduct and behavior that students observe and may emulate
questions.explanation: Teachers model values and behavior that students often imitate, making personal conduct an important part of the role.

questions.question: Which of these best distinguishes teaching from a 'semi-profession' in classical sociological classification?
options: Teaching has full autonomy comparable to medicine and law in every jurisdiction
Some scholars classify teaching as a semi-profession due to variable autonomy and standardization across contexts
Teaching requires no ethical code
Teaching has never had any professional body anywhere
questions.correct_answer: Some scholars classify teaching as a semi-profession due to variable autonomy and standardization across contexts
questions.explanation: Some sociologists classify teaching as a 'semi-profession' because its degree of autonomy and standardized entry requirements can vary more than in professions like medicine or law.

questions.question: Continuous professional development for teachers is important mainly because it:
options: Is legally required but has no real benefit
Helps teachers update their knowledge, skills, and teaching methods over time
Reduces the number of qualified teachers
Eliminates the need for initial teacher training
questions.correct_answer: Helps teachers update their knowledge, skills, and teaching methods over time
questions.explanation: Ongoing professional development keeps teachers current with new knowledge, curricula, and instructional techniques.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the relationship between teacher licensing and professional standards?
options: Licensing ensures only qualified and vetted individuals practice as teachers, upholding standards
Licensing has no connection to professional standards
Anyone can be licensed to teach without any qualification
Licensing is only required for university lecturers
questions.correct_answer: Licensing ensures only qualified and vetted individuals practice as teachers, upholding standards
questions.explanation: Licensing through bodies like TRCN screens practitioners for qualification and conduct, helping to maintain professional standards.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'commitment' as a professional value expected of teachers?
options: Dedication to the growth and success of learners and the profession
Working only the minimum required hours
Avoiding all extracurricular responsibilities
Focusing solely on personal financial gain
questions.correct_answer: Dedication to the growth and success of learners and the profession
questions.explanation: Professional commitment reflects a teacher's dedication to student learning and the advancement of the teaching profession.

questions.question: The National Policy on Education in Nigeria addresses teacher education mainly to:
options: Standardize and improve the quality of teacher preparation nationwide
Abolish the need for teacher training institutions
Restrict education to only urban areas
Eliminate professional bodies overseeing teachers
questions.correct_answer: Standardize and improve the quality of teacher preparation nationwide
questions.explanation: The National Policy on Education sets guidelines aimed at improving and standardizing teacher preparation across the country.

questions.question: Which of the following is an appropriate professional response when a teacher is uncertain about content they are to teach?
options: Guess and present incorrect information confidently
Research, consult resources, or seek guidance before teaching the content
Skip the topic without informing students
Ask students to teach the topic to themselves with no guidance
questions.correct_answer: Research, consult resources, or seek guidance before teaching the content
questions.explanation: Professional integrity requires teachers to ensure accuracy of content, seeking clarification rather than presenting unverified information.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'de-registration' by TRCN?
options: A routine annual renewal process for all teachers
The removal of a teacher's name from the professional register due to serious misconduct or unfitness to practice
A promotion given to outstanding teachers
A scholarship awarded to teacher trainees
questions.correct_answer: The removal of a teacher's name from the professional register due to serious misconduct or unfitness to practice
questions.explanation: De-registration is a disciplinary action where a teacher is struck off the professional register, typically for gross misconduct or malpractice.

questions.question: Which of the following is a reason teaching requires continuous mastery of subject content?
options: Knowledge and curricula evolve, so teachers must stay updated to teach effectively
Subject content never changes once learned
Students do not benefit from an informed teacher
Mastery of content is irrelevant to teaching quality
questions.correct_answer: Knowledge and curricula evolve, so teachers must stay updated to teach effectively
questions.explanation: Because knowledge, technology, and curricula change over time, teachers must continually update their subject mastery to teach effectively.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why patience is considered an essential quality for teachers?
options: Learners progress at different paces and teachers must guide them without frustration
Patience allows teachers to ignore lesson planning
Patience is only needed for teaching young children
Patience has no effect on classroom outcomes
questions.correct_answer: Learners progress at different paces and teachers must guide them without frustration
questions.explanation: Because students learn at different rates, patience helps teachers support struggling learners effectively without discouraging them.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a teacher fulfilling the role of 'agent of socialization'?
options: Teaching students societal norms, values, and acceptable behavior alongside academic content
Refusing to interact with students outside academic subjects
Avoiding discussion of moral or civic values
Focusing exclusively on examination scores
questions.correct_answer: Teaching students societal norms, values, and acceptable behavior alongside academic content
questions.explanation: Teachers help socialize learners into the norms and values of society, extending their role beyond pure academics.

questions.question: Which of the following most accurately describes why teaching is sometimes called the 'mother of all professions'?
options: Because it existed before written history and produces practitioners of all other professions
Because teachers earn the highest salaries
Because it requires no formal training
Because teachers control government policy
questions.correct_answer: Because it existed before written history and produces practitioners of all other professions
questions.explanation: Teaching is often called the mother of all professions because every professional, including doctors and lawyers, was first trained by teachers.

questions.question: Which of the following describes an appropriate teacher response to a student's classroom misbehavior?
options: Applying fair, consistent, and constructive disciplinary measures aligned with school policy
Publicly humiliating the student in front of peers
Using physical violence to punish the student
Ignoring the behavior even when it disrupts learning
questions.correct_answer: Applying fair, consistent, and constructive disciplinary measures aligned with school policy
questions.explanation: Professional and ethical classroom management calls for fair, consistent discipline that supports learning rather than humiliation or excessive punishment.

questions.question: Which best describes 'confidentiality' as an ethical obligation for teachers?
options: Protecting sensitive student information from inappropriate disclosure
Refusing to communicate with parents at all
Hiding academic performance from school authorities
Sharing students' personal records publicly
questions.correct_answer: Protecting sensitive student information from inappropriate disclosure
questions.explanation: Confidentiality requires teachers to safeguard private student information and disclose it only when appropriate and necessary.

questions.question: Why is regulation of the teaching profession by a body like TRCN considered important for society?
options: It ensures only competent, ethical individuals are allowed to teach, protecting learners
It increases the number of unqualified teachers in schools
It has no impact on the quality of education
It replaces the need for teacher training entirely
questions.correct_answer: It ensures only competent, ethical individuals are allowed to teach, protecting learners
questions.explanation: Professional regulation protects learners and the public by ensuring only qualified, ethical practitioners are permitted to teach.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the idea of teaching as 'a profession of service'?
options: Teachers primarily work to serve the learning needs and development of students and society
Teachers work exclusively to maximize personal profit
Teaching offers no benefit to the wider community
Service in teaching refers only to serving meals in schools
questions.correct_answer: Teachers primarily work to serve the learning needs and development of students and society
questions.explanation: Teaching is regarded as a service profession because its central purpose is to serve the developmental and learning needs of students and society.

questions.question: Which of the following is a professional obligation teachers have towards colleagues?
options: Undermining colleagues to gain favor with school administration
Collaborating respectfully and supporting collegial professional growth
Refusing to share teaching resources under any circumstance
Publicly criticizing colleagues in front of students
questions.correct_answer: Collaborating respectfully and supporting collegial professional growth
questions.explanation: Professional ethics call for teachers to treat colleagues with respect and support a collaborative working environment.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why teacher training includes both subject content and pedagogy (methods of teaching)?
options: Knowing content alone is insufficient; teachers must also know how to effectively deliver it to learners
Pedagogy is unnecessary if a teacher knows the subject
Subject content is irrelevant once teaching methods are mastered
Only one of the two is ever taught in teacher training programs
questions.correct_answer: Knowing content alone is insufficient; teachers must also know how to effectively deliver it to learners
questions.explanation: Effective teaching requires both mastery of subject content and pedagogical skill to communicate that content to learners of varying abilities.

questions.question: Which of the following best illustrates the concept of 'professional autonomy' for teachers?
options: Teachers having some independent judgment in instructional decisions within professional and ethical bounds
Teachers being completely unsupervised with no accountability
Teachers having no say in how they teach
Autonomy meaning teachers set their own salaries
questions.correct_answer: Teachers having some independent judgment in instructional decisions within professional and ethical bounds
questions.explanation: Professional autonomy refers to the reasonable latitude teachers have to exercise judgment in instructional matters, while remaining accountable to standards.

questions.question: Which of these best describes why teaching is often undervalued relative to its societal importance in some contexts?
options: A mismatch between the profession's critical societal role and the recognition/compensation it receives
Because teaching has no societal importance
Because there are too few students to teach
Because teaching requires no skill
questions.correct_answer: A mismatch between the profession's critical societal role and the recognition/compensation it receives
questions.explanation: Despite its foundational role in national development, teaching is sometimes undervalued through inadequate pay and low social recognition relative to its importance.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate way for a beginning teacher to build professional competence?
options: Avoiding feedback from experienced colleagues and supervisors
Seeking mentorship, reflecting on practice, and pursuing further training
Refusing to attend workshops or seminars
Relying only on knowledge gained many years prior with no updates
questions.correct_answer: Seeking mentorship, reflecting on practice, and pursuing further training
questions.explanation: New teachers build competence through mentorship, reflective practice, and ongoing professional development.

questions.question: Which best describes the difference between a teacher's role as 'instructor' versus 'mentor'?
options: Instructor focuses on delivering content and skills; mentor provides broader guidance and support for personal growth
There is no difference between the two roles
A mentor only grades examinations
An instructor never interacts with students directly
questions.correct_answer: Instructor focuses on delivering content and skills; mentor provides broader guidance and support for personal growth
questions.explanation: While instruction emphasizes content delivery, mentoring extends to guiding students' broader personal and professional development.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why fairness and impartiality are emphasized in teacher ethics?
options: To ensure all students are treated equitably regardless of background or personal bias
To allow teachers to favor high-performing students only
Because fairness has no bearing on student trust
To justify unequal grading practices
questions.correct_answer: To ensure all students are treated equitably regardless of background or personal bias
questions.explanation: Fairness and impartiality ensure that all students receive equitable treatment and opportunities, free from favoritism or discrimination.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes why the teaching profession requires periodic re-certification or continuous registration in some jurisdictions?
options: To ensure teachers remain qualified, competent, and in good professional standing over time
To generate revenue with no professional purpose
Because certification never expires under any system
To exclude experienced teachers from the profession
questions.correct_answer: To ensure teachers remain qualified, competent, and in good professional standing over time
questions.explanation: Periodic registration/renewal processes help ensure teachers maintain competence and good standing throughout their careers.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a key benefit of respecting cultural and individual diversity in the classroom?
options: It fosters an inclusive learning environment where all students feel valued
It slows down the pace of learning unnecessarily
It has no effect on student engagement
It only benefits the teacher, not the students
questions.correct_answer: It fosters an inclusive learning environment where all students feel valued
questions.explanation: Respecting diversity helps create an inclusive classroom climate that supports engagement and learning for all students.

questions.question: Which best summarizes the overall aim of a course such as 'Valuing the Teaching Profession'?
options: To help prospective teachers understand, appreciate, and commit to the standards and value of the teaching profession
To train students exclusively in unrelated technical skills
To discourage students from pursuing teaching careers
To focus only on examination techniques with no professional content
questions.correct_answer: To help prospective teachers understand, appreciate, and commit to the standards and value of the teaching profession
questions.explanation: Such a course aims to build students' understanding of, and commitment to, the value, ethics, and standards of the teaching profession.
